question: Measures to reduce workers’ wages or benefits during periods of sick leave or justified absence are being considered in the public debate in some countries. These proposals present illness as a cost or abuse, without differentiating between fraudulent cases, recognised temporary incapacity, legitimate leave, caring for family members or mental health issues.

Directive 89/391/EEC requires that the safety and health of workers be ensured in every aspect related to their work. Article 31 of the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights recognises the right of every worker to conditions which respect his or her health, safety and dignity. In light of the above: 1.
Does the Commission consider it compatible with the European acquis on health and safety at work to penalise workers financially during duly recognised sick leave?

Does it agree that imposing financial penalties for medical absences, including those resulting from ordinary circumstances, can put pressure on workers to return to work before they are fully recovered, putting their physical and mental health at risk and weakening the effective protection of their health at work?
Will it ensure that the Quality Jobs Act promotes an approach based on prevention, mental health, workplace adaptation and social dialogue, rather than punitive measures in response to illness?
